translationRepairs: He was moved to Bozhou, made Northwest Circuit Pacification Commissioner, and then promoted to Commissioner of the Wugu Shilei tribal command.
He was moved to Bozhou, made Assistant Pacification Commissioner of the Northwest Circuit, and then promoted to Commissioner of the Wugu Shilei tribal command.
西北路招討都監 is the assistant/supervisory pacification post (都監), not the full 招討使. The original English drops 都監.
He was transferred to Bozhou, changed to Northwest Circuit Pacification Commissioner, and promoted to Commissioner of the Wugu Shilei Tribal Command.
He was transferred to Bozhou, changed to Northwest Circuit Assistant Pacification Commissioner, and promoted to Commissioner of the Wugu Shilei Tribal Command.
The literal likewise renders 招討都監 as a full pacification commissioner; Assistant Pacification Commissioner restores 都監.

When the court sent Grand Councilor Pusans Zhongyi to replace Mouyan in command, Xiang again followed Zhongyi in pursuit to Xianquan west of Niaoling. He overtook the enemy, led the right wing in a personal charge, and routed them so completely that men and horses trampled one another to death; Xianquan was nearly cleared.

When the court sent Grand Councilor Pusan Zhongyi to replace Mouyan in command, Xiang again followed Zhongyi in pursuit to Xianquan west of Niaoling. He overtook the enemy, led the right wing in a personal charge, and routed them so completely that men and horses trampled one another to death; Xianquan was nearly cleared.
僕散 is the Jurchen surname Pusan; Pusans wrongly pluralizes it.

It happened that the court sent the Grand Councilor Pusans Zhongyi to replace Mouyan as commander; Xiang again followed Zhongyi in pursuing the rebels to Xianquan west of Niaoling, overtook them, led the right wing and charged ahead in person; the rebels were greatly routed, men and horses trampling one another to death; Xianquan was nearly pacified.

It happened that the court sent the Grand Councilor Pusan Zhongyi to replace Mouyan as commander; Xiang again followed Zhongyi in pursuing the rebels to Xianquan west of Niaoling, overtook them, led the right wing and charged ahead in person; the rebels were greatly routed, men and horses trampling one another to death; Xianquan was nearly pacified.
The same 僕散忠義 must be Pusan Zhongyi in the literal field, not Pusans.

When Song sued for peace and the army withdrew, he was summoned as Commander of the Archway Guard Direct, made Right Guard General of the Hall Army, then Left Guard General, sent out as Northeast Circuit Pacification Commissioner, promoted to Commissioner of the Supin Circuit, and finally transferred to Commander-in-Chief of Yilan Circuit forces.

When Song sued for peace and the army withdrew, he was summoned as Commander of the Archway Guard Direct, made Right Guard General of the Hall Army, then Left Guard General, sent out as Northeast Circuit Assistant Pacification Commissioner, promoted to Commissioner of the Supin Circuit, and finally transferred to Commander-in-Chief of Yilan Circuit forces.
東北路招討都監 is the assistant pacification post, not the full commissioner. The parenthetical (dujian) is awkward in idiomatic English; Assistant Pacification Commissioner restores 都監 without a gloss.
Shizong, the principal imperial grandson of the Prince of Jinyuan, was to receive a princely title, and the court ordered a state name chosen for the enfeoffment.
Because the Prince of Jinyuan was the principal imperial grandson, Shizong was about to confer a princely title on him, and an edict ordered a state name chosen for the enfeoffment.

世宗以金源郡王世嫡皇孫，將加王爵 makes Shizong the actor and the Prince of Jinyuan, the principal imperial grandson, the recipient. The original inverts that kinship; the proposal’s “taking the Prince of Jinyuan” is a stiff calque of 以.
Shizong, as the principal imperial grandson of the Prince of Jinyuan, was about to be granted princely rank, and an edict was issued to select a state name.
Shizong, taking the Prince of Jinyuan as the principal imperial grandson, was about to confer princely rank, and an edict was issued to select a state name.
The literal correctly restores Shizong as the one conferring rank on the Prince of Jinyuan, the 世嫡皇孫, rather than making Shizong the grandson.

On his return Shizong questioned him about frontier affairs. Xiang submitted detailed maps and proposed policies to keep dependent tribes loyal and to subdue Dashi of the Qara Khitai. The emperor ordered all of it carried out.

On his return Shizong questioned him about frontier affairs. Xiang submitted detailed maps and proposed policies to keep dependent tribes loyal and to hold the Dashi (Qara Khitai) in check. The emperor ordered all of it carried out.
鎮服大石 names the Dashi/Qara Khitai regime, not a living individual “Dashi of the Qara Khitai.”
The eastern force reached the Longju River and was surrounded by Beizu Xu. Trapped for three days, it sent urgent appeals for help. Some urged Xiang to wait until the full army had gathered.
The eastern force reached the Longju River and was surrounded by the Zuxu. Trapped for three days, it sent urgent appeals for help. Some urged waiting until the full army had gathered.

為阻珝所圍 and 或請俟諸軍集乃發 name the Zuxu and an unnamed request to wait; Beizu Xu invents a personal name, and Zu Xu still treats 阻珝 as an individual. The same juan’s 北阻珝 shows a people. Removing the invented vocative Xiang is right.

In the tenth month Beizu Xu rebelled again, and Xiang marched out to encamp at Beijing. At the same time the Khitan herding-office leaders Deshou and Tuosuo seized Xizhou, declared a reign title of Shengsheng, and claimed an army of hundreds of thousands, throwing the region into alarm.

In the tenth month the Zuxu rebelled again, and Xiang marched out to encamp at Beijing. At the same time the Khitan herding-office leaders Deshou and Tuosuo seized Xinzhou, declared a reign title of Shensheng, and claimed an army of hundreds of thousands, throwing the region into alarm.
身聖 is Shensheng, not Shengsheng, and 阻珝 is the Zuxu people, not Beizu Xu. The proposal still leaves 信州 as Xizhou; 信州 is Xinzhou.

In the tenth month Beizu Xu rebelled again; Xiang went out to encamp at Beijing; meanwhile the herding-office Khitan Deshou, Tuosuo, and others seized Xizhou in rebellion, falsely establishing an era title called Shengsheng, claiming hundreds of thousands of followers, and all near and far were shaken.

In the tenth month the Zuxu rebelled again; Xiang went out to encamp at Beijing; meanwhile the herding-office Khitan Deshou, Tuosuo, and others seized Xinzhou in rebellion, falsely establishing an era title called Shensheng, claiming hundreds of thousands of followers, and all near and far were shaken.
The literal must likewise read 阻珝 as the Zuxu, 身聖 as Shensheng, and 信州 as Xinzhou.
The following year he left office to observe mourning for a close relative.
The following year he left office to observe mourning for his mother.
內艱 is the conventional term for mourning a mother, not an unspecified close relative.

As a northern campaign was debated, Xiang proposed sending Zonghao, Deputy Director of the Great Closer-of-Kin Office, to lead troops from Taizhou; sending Left Vice Minister Heng to establish a mobile Military Affairs Commission at Fuzhou to march Northwest Circuit forces against Beizu Xu; and leading his own army out from Linhuang.

As a northern campaign was debated, Xiang proposed sending Zonghao, Deputy Director of the Great Closer-of-Kin Office, to lead troops from Taizhou; sending Left Vice Minister Heng to establish a mobile Military Affairs Commission at Fuzhou to march Northwest Circuit forces to intercept the Zuxu; and leading his own army out from Linhuang.

邀阻珝 is intercepting the Zuxu as a people, not a person Beizu Xu. Wikisource and Chinese Notes both print 阻珝 (and 北阻珝) in this juan, so the received text is not 阻卜; emending to Zubu is unsupported by those witnesses.

A drought was then afflicting the realm. The court ordered the relevant offices to pray for rain, and Xiang, together with Grand Chancellor Zhang Wannu, Vice Grand Chancellor Pusan Kui, and others submitted memorials accepting blame.

A drought was then afflicting the realm. The court ordered the relevant offices to pray for rain, and Xiang, together with Grand Chancellor Zhang Wangong, Vice Grand Chancellor Pusan Kui, and others submitted memorials accepting blame.
張萬公 is Zhang Wangong; Wannu misreads 萬公.
Jiagu Heng, whose original name was Alibu, came from the Sandu Meng'an Yida baimouke in Shandong West Circuit.
Jiagu Heng, whose original name was Alibu, came from the Santu Meng'an Yida baimouke in Shandong West Circuit.
三土 is Santu, not Sandu.
Jiagu Heng, original name Alibu, was a man of the Sandu Meng'an Yida baimouke in Shandong West Circuit.
Jiagu Heng, original name Alibu, was a man of the Santu Meng'an Yida baimouke in Shandong West Circuit.
The literal must likewise transcribe 三土 as Santu.

Heng said: "If it were merely profitable, the ancients would already have practiced it. Moreover, it requires much labor for little planted area; I also fear wasteland would be abandoned and the people would toil in vain without benefit."

Heng said: "If it were truly profitable, the ancients would already have practiced it. Moreover, it requires much labor for little planted area; I also fear farmland would be left waste and the people would toil in vain without benefit."
荒廢土田 is cultivated land going to waste, not abandoning wasteland. The proposal still keeps “merely” for 若苟有利, which is “if it were indeed/truly profitable,” as the idiomatic already has.
He was twice promoted, to Deputy Commissioner of the Ceremonial Guard Bureau.
He was promoted again to Deputy Commissioner of the Ceremonial Guard Bureau.
再遷 marks a further promotion, not two promotions into that office.
In the first year of Taihe he was specially granted the hereditary meng'an of Yanyan River in the Southwest Circuit, concurrently hezha baimouke.
In the first year of Taihe he was specially granted the hereditary meng'an of Yanyan River in the Southwest Circuit, concurrently hezha mouke.
合劄謀克 is a hezha mouke; baimouke fuses in 把, which is not in this title.
In the first year of Taihe he was specially granted the hereditary meng'an of Yanyan River in the Southwest Circuit, concurrently hezha baimouke.
In the first year of Taihe he was specially granted the hereditary meng'an of Yanyan River in the Southwest Circuit, concurrently hezha mouke.
The literal likewise must read 合劄謀克 as hezha mouke, not baimouke.
Yaoli Beidie came from the Tuoluo Mountain meng'an in the Kubai meng'an district of the Beijing Circuit.
Yaoli Beidie came from the Tuoluo Mountain mouke under the Kubai meng'an of the Beijing Circuit.
陀羅山謀克 is a mouke under the 窟白猛安; calling Tuoluo Mountain a meng'an collapses the two offices.
Yaoli Beidie was a man of the Tuoluo Mountain meng'an in Kubai meng'an, Beijing Circuit.
Yaoli Beidie was a man of the Tuoluo Mountain mouke in the Kubai meng'an, Beijing Circuit.
The literal must distinguish 窟白猛安 from 陀羅山謀克.

In the second year of Cheng'an more than a thousand Khitan horsemen raided back and forth between Jin and Yi. Beidie pursued and defeated them, recovered the booty, and returned everything to the original households.

In the second year of Cheng'an more than a thousand horsemen raided back and forth between Jinzhou and Yizhou. Beidie pursued and defeated them, recovered the booty, and returned everything to the original households.
錦、懿 are Jinzhou and Yizhou, and the preceding unit camps at 懿州. Bare “Jin” reads as the dynasty. The proposal still calls 颭軍 “Khitan”; that ethnicity is not in this sentence.

In the second year of Cheng'an, more than a thousand Khitan troops appeared and vanished raiding between Jin and Yi; Beidie pursued and defeated them, recovered what had been plundered, and returned it all to the original households.

In the second year of Cheng'an, more than a thousand troops appeared and vanished raiding between Jinzhou and Yizhou; Beidie pursued and defeated them, recovered what had been plundered, and returned it all to the original households.
The literal must likewise take 錦、懿 as Jinzhou and Yizhou, and 颭軍 is not Khitan.
In the third year he followed Associate Director of the Great Mujin Office Zonghao as commander of the left wing, fought at the Yimi River, and won;
In the third year he followed Associate Director of the Great Court of the Imperial Clan Zonghao as commander of the left wing, fought at the Yimi River, and won;
大睦親府 is the court of imperial-clan affairs; Mujin is a false reading of 睦親.
The encomium says: In the first six of the Army hexagram in the Changes: "The army sets forth according to discipline; ill fortune and harm follow."
The encomium says: In the first yin line of the Army hexagram in the Changes: "The army sets forth according to discipline; ill fortune and harm follow."
初六 is the first yin line of the hexagram, not “first six.” The parenthetical (chu liu) is unnecessary once that is stated.
